actualReleaseList.body:
# source-v2.1.0-rc.15 — Develop the strategy. Preserve the mission.

Bring a real business opportunity or a frontier mathematics question to
[SUCCESSOR Ω Mission Studio](https://montrealai.github.io/AGIJobsv0/successor/mission/).
Define the outcome worth pursuing, ground the work in public evidence, and retain
the strategies and experiments needed to judge the next attempt. Mission Studio
is the primary English/French flagship journey; it prepares an exact native
Computer Use task and a reusable mission record without an account, wallet or
API key.

Production approval remains **false**. This is an unsigned source and evidence
prerelease. Browser exports and native Jobs work orders remain unsigned,
unfunded drafts. A mission record creates no purchasing, payment, computer,
signing or blockchain authority.

## Start with work that matters to you

The Studio starts from the user's actual mission: a business opportunity or a
mathematics research question, the current approach, the best credible
alternative, a hard outcome and its constraints, public source URLs and the
evidence text supplied with them. The record distinguishes user-supplied
evidence from an independently checked source. A URL or pasted excerpt alone
does not establish correctness, permission, freshness or a successful result.

Seal those inputs into one mission before preparing the experiment. Keep
strategy candidates, comparisons, rejected attempts, proposed changes and
results in the experiment and strategy ledger. Reuse that record for the next
attempt while preserving the original mission identity. This supplies a
concrete research workspace and handoff; it does not claim that a browser form
has executed research, discovered a business advantage or solved a frontier
mathematics problem.

The Level 3 task asks a computer-using worker to develop and compare strategies,
including the current approach and credible alternative, and retain the evidence
for its choice. The Level 4 task makes a proposed reformulation explicit for an
owner decision. The hard outcome and actual constraints remain binding; an
unapproved change cannot quietly become the new mission. A mathematical
conjecture, numerical example or model assertion remains a claim until the
appropriate checks establish it. No mathematical breakthrough or independently
proven AI Alpha is asserted by this release.

The handoff uses the owned, exact-source Alpha70 native `ComputerTask` contract,
a keyboard-and-mouse browser workspace with an explicit source URL allowlist,
and a ChatGPT Work operator prompt. The package carries the sealed mission and
reusable evidence record into a separately authorized worker session. Preparing
or downloading it does not execute that session, authenticate a model's result
or commission a provider. GitHub Pages accepts no API key and performs no live
provider qualification. Four native Jobs drafts reserve **zero AGIALPHA** and
remain unsigned and unfunded; review, funding and execution require separate
owner decisions.

Large valid research records remain available for complete export and restore
even when they exceed native task or browser-link capacity. The operator handoff
then requires the exact exported package and both content digests. Native Alpha
HTML admission stays at 200,000 characters; the separate bounded portable format
supports all accepted field sizes and escaping with a shared UTF-8 export/import
limit. The interface makes session-only updates and export-before-closing clear.

## Reproduce a bounded strategy comparison

The [supplier Computer Use laboratory](https://montrealai.github.io/AGIJobsv0/successor/computer/)
is a secondary validation example. Its disclosed arithmetic and real browser
protocol exercise make the distinction between a proposed strategy, an observed
interaction and independent proof inspectable before using the separate Studio
handoff for a real mission.

The disclosed fictional buyer needs 40 units: at least 10 by day 7 and all 40 by
day 14, within USD 510.00. Buying all 40 from Stellar costs USD 490.00. A staged
recommendation buys 10 from Stellar and 30 from Laurentian for USD 360.00,
including both suppliers' shipping charges. The USD 130.00 difference is exact
arithmetic on synthetic offers, not observed customer savings or a claim about
real inventory, delivery or procurement.

**Level 3 develops the strategy itself.** The engine constructs typed programs
from a finite grammar with 24 combinations of allocation, ordering and cost
operators, with up to two failure-driven revisions. Each attempt retains its
program, execution, logical-operation use, result and lineage. A candidate is
frozen before two distinct generated public fresh cases are evaluated. A
changed candidate needs a new record. These inspectable cases are not protected
independent holdouts, and the bounded grammar does not establish open-ended
strategy invention.

**Level 4 examines an extra assumption.** A local, explicit comparison can relax
the extra assumption that all units must come from one supplier or arrive early.
The buyer's actual quantities, deadlines, budget and recommendation-only scope
remain fixed and checked. If all 40 units really are required by day 7, a late
shipment remains invalid and the USD 490.00 feasible incumbent remains the
comparison. This is bounded outcome-preserving reformulation, not a claim of
general transformational intelligence.

A credible conventional two-delivery comparison also finds USD 360.00. The
constructed strategy therefore establishes **no same-task superiority** over
that alternative and no independently proven AI Alpha. The USD 490.00-to-360.00
comparison changes the additional workflow assumption. The institutional
decision remains `INCUMBENT_RETAINED_PENDING_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW`; a useful
nominee does not authorize replacement.

The public supplier desk accepts keyboard and mouse interaction, recomputes
quantities, shipping, deadlines and budget, and displays the exact observed
allocation result. Keep the readable brief, program lineage, frozen comparison,
fresh-case results and mission together. Reopening a report replays its
bindings. A checksum does not authenticate an author, provider or reviewer;
imported execution claims cannot grant authority or become independent proof.

## Computer use with attributable limits

The separate local laboratory uses the exact-source Alpha integration and real
Chromium. Its default adviser supplies scripted native Responses `computer_call`
batches; actual browser actions and screenshots exercise the screenshot/action
transport and the observed allocation check. A scripted adviser does not
demonstrate a live foundation model discovering the plan or completing the task
independently. Provider usage and billing remain unknown for this fixture.

The preparation route exports the frozen task, standalone desk and an operator
prompt for a separately authorized ChatGPT Work session with browser or computer
access. The native Alpha `ComputerTask` export retains the exact mission,
report, frozen program, plan and HTML bindings. The operator route remains
separate from the scripted rehearsal: current account access, model support,
provider compatibility, isolation and exact-task admission require their own
qualification. The GitHub Pages mission neither accepts API keys nor calls a
live model provider. A copied prompt does not connect or commission a worker.

Reproduce the local route using the documented explicit Alpha source, Node and
Chromium paths, or use `--prepare-only` to inspect the package before contacting
any provider. Keep credentials in the local operator environment. The
[Computer Use guide](../successor/COMPUTER_USE_LEVELS.md) explains the exact
commands, evidence classes and separate operator route. The public interface's
English and French paths retain the same mission and evidence boundaries.

The dedicated `successor-computer.yml` workflow is a new required source-release
gate. It exercises the real browser protocol fixture on the exact source; its
scripted result remains scoped to transport and the bounded task. Publication
still requires that workflow, every other required workflow, every observed
main-push workflow and all required checks to succeed on the exact merged SHA.
No unproduced fixture result is embedded in these notes or added to the release
asset inventory.

## Keep useful work through the existing journey

The exact Alpha laboratory mirror remains pinned to
`70dac8e5ce739978f5cd96d0fc190b6ebfcdf8d7`, with its source, executable-code and
license inventory. The public-source mission still compares six extractive
methods, retains exact source passages, freezes one method and checks a distinct
user-attested fresh source. Its checks remain mechanical and its independent
proof remains unestablished. Native Jobs compiler handoffs retain zero assigned
funding and require owner decisions; AGIALPHA allowances and Manager USDC
pricing stay separate.

Mission Studio leads that research-to-usefulness journey; the supplier
laboratory supplies a bounded validation example, and the retained catalog
provides further experiences. **Alpha** is the advantage worth pursuing. The
**Gym** develops methods. **Specialist ASI** requires earned
mission-specific superiority on agreed fresh protected work. **SUCCESSOR Ω**
preserves useful methods and memory after proof and explicit bounded
authorization. This laboratory awards no Specialist ASI designation.

## Published history and current deployment evidence

The [published rc.14 release](https://github.com/MontrealAI/AGIJobsv0/releases/tag/source-v2.1.0-rc.14)
remains at `fecde507f770481bfd68efddcb92230a0d885b53`, tree
`de0c98780babc193fa62efeceda5df4278fc6b21`. Its tag and all fifteen assets are
immutable. Its original notes remain byte for byte unchanged, with SHA-256
`7cf35c789d6bc61f5e96a12542a8fd8dd1f1f38be2ab1b97d301f3304909c233`.
Its main-push qualification completed 39 workflows successfully, with 114
successful checks, two expected skips and all 33 required contexts successful.
That is evidence about rc.14; rc.15 requires its own exact-source qualification.
The rc.13 proposal remains explicitly unpublished. Published rc.12 and every
earlier tag, asset and historical note receipt remain unchanged.

The retained directory still records the five-contract 18 October Alpha suite
from source `c0fc5217e364a39a4cd123d17a8317c06b80f820` and the 25-contract Jobs
deployment from source `818b3a246871e4cd4dde86558dbb91ef82b15eef`, tree
`b1c3bb0f4b8d64e0d23376d6b6ef3722c4c67b0d`. The Jobs snapshot remains pinned to
[publication 284351148d96c5390a655aec1f9db806284f2400](https://github.com/MontrealAI/AGIJobsv0/blob/284351148d96c5390a655aec1f9db806284f2400/docs/production/mainnet-2026-10-18/deployment-snapshot.json),
with exact raw SHA-256
`b4335f5763f73e8da664c3cd45ac7ca8fa6f0d3beb2780b209e50fd1e3def23f`.
It records 25 runtime matches, 25 source-metadata matches, 46 named state checks,
no creator ownership among the 25 contracts, and all eight managed modules
paused. Its state anchor is provider-reported finalized block 26221285, hash
`0x4bd7698479db125e9a7e4f031571fd2844224f822a630ba22b40aea48fb592e6`.
Explorer source readback is separately timed and not block pinned. The dated
guide and 39 successful historical receipts preserve their declared scope.

This release performs no fresh live deployment check and does not assume
current-main equivalence with the separately deployed Jobs source. The 12
October rc.4 source, addresses and protected historical assets remain intact.
Named getters and absent creator ownership do not prove exhaustive historical,
indirect or external authority. Public activation remains unapproved; the Alpha
suite has no global pause.

## Compiler, source and publication gates

No Jobs Solidity, deployment writer, ABI, constructor, settlement rule or
dependency identity changes. The strict reviewed compiler-source baseline
remains `3c17153942251116ee51163055eb1a25d652454b`; preserved deployment evidence
remains bound to `9c730e0188594089e27ed0589c2b5ca57eec5cf5` and deployed-source
ancestry to `b4c5b66ea05a6bb27f1f1cb197f055c179bbd38e`. Protected path arrays,
source exclusions and fail-closed policy remain unchanged. The compiler remains
native Solidity `0.8.37+commit.f401782d`, Cancun, via-IR, 200 optimizer runs and
IPFS metadata. Existing collateral, eligibility, reputation, bounded authority
handover/recovery and disposable-caller policies retain their reviewed scope.

The fifteen release assets contain **14 checksummed payloads** plus
`SHA256SUMS.txt`: the exact source archive; source provenance; these notes;
authenticated compiler ZIP and producer provenance; compiler policy and warning
guide; the unchanged historical deployment/configuration records, addressbook
and guide; and the separate current Jobs snapshot, dated deployment guide and
39-receipt projection. The current snapshot appears once as
`jobs-mainnet-2026-10-18.json`. Both canonical and website copies must match its
immutable digest. Standalone guide links bind the immutable publication commit.
Recomputed release checksums cannot replace pinned snapshot bytes or authentic
compiler-producer bytes. No fixture-proof asset is added.

Publication requires an authentic successful exact merged-source compiler
producer, all 15 required workflow paths, all 33 required contexts and every
observed main-push workflow. It verifies the tag, producer identities, complete
asset inventory and every downloaded checksum. Same-SHA retries may resume;
existing tags and assets are never moved or replaced. RC14's 14 checksum rows
remain evidence of that immutable release, not payloads to be rewritten for
rc.15.

Production signing, independent security review, provider/worker commissioning,
complete authority evidence and explicit activation authorization remain
separate gates. External audit and Sepolia remain **NOT PERFORMED —
OWNER-ACCEPTED OMISSION**. Local tests, hosted CI and AI-assisted review are not
an external security audit. Previous deployments remain outside the mutation
scope. This publisher sends no real-wallet signature, public deployment,
funding, token movement, settlement, procurement or unpause transaction.

# source-v2.1.0-rc.14 — Find your Alpha. Build your SUCCESSOR Ω.

Start free with a reproducible laboratory, use public sources to develop a real
mission, then retain the methods and evidence for reuse. This flagship brings the
Alpha experience into AGI Jobs while preserving the difference between useful
local work, measured evidence, independent proof and authorized operation.

Production approval remains **false**. This is a source and evidence prerelease.
Browser downloads and native Jobs work orders remain unsigned, unfunded drafts;
all eight managed modules remain paused in the retained deployment observation.

This publication consolidates the flagship preparation from PR #3989, the rc.13
preparation and documentation history from PRs #3985/#3984, and PR #3988's current
public deployment records. **rc.13 was not tagged or published**. Its
[unpublished proposal](https://github.com/MontrealAI/AGIJobsv0/blob/source-v2.1.0-rc.14/docs/production/RELEASE_NOTES_SOURCE_RC13.md) remains explicitly historical;
the new publication identity is `source-v2.1.0-rc.14`. Published rc.12 and every
earlier tag and asset remain unchanged.

## A useful first mission, with a record worth keeping

The English/French browser journey includes the native Alpha catalog laboratory
and a guided source-grounded mission. A user can compare competing methods, keep
the incumbent where improvement is unestablished, and download the outputs,
methods and history. The free browser work requires no account, wallet or model
API. It does not submit transactions.

The source-grounded mission works with bounded public text supplied by the user.
Six bounded extraction methods compare passages against the declared goal, with
an opening-passage incumbent, goal-word/coverage heuristics, omission searching,
and random/sham controls under the same sentence-count budget. Exact offsets
bind every quotation to its stored source. The user freezes one method before
checking a distinct, user-attested fresh source. The history retains source
commitments, comparisons, annotations and recorded review decisions for reuse.
Source URLs are user attribution; the browser does not fetch or authenticate them.
Freshness, rights and reviewer labels remain self-attested. These mechanical checks
do not verify
that a source is true or establish expert correctness, a business advantage,
independent superiority or Specialist ASI. The institutional decision remains
**HOLD**; no browser result grants operational authority.

Advanced details follow the user's next action. The user can retain a downloadable
mission record and prepare four bounded source-mission work orders with the
actual native Jobs compiler. Those orders have zero assigned AGIALPHA budget and
placeholder roles requiring an owner decision. The catalog mission's separate
handoff supports an explicit AGIALPHA allowance in exact base units. Manager USDC
drafts remain separately priced; there is no implied conversion or payment.
Existing demos and flowcharts remain available.

The Alpha laboratory mirror is bound to upstream commit
`70dac8e5ce739978f5cd96d0fc190b6ebfcdf8d7`. Its checked provenance records the
original page and source inventory, unchanged executable code and the explicit
navigation-only changes needed to serve it from the Jobs website. Source and
license inventories retain Alpha's Apache 2.0 material and the MIT native Jobs
compiler components. The new Jobs mission is separately identified from that
retained mirror.

## Current contract records, with their scope intact

The public ecosystem directory now points to the **18 October 2026 Alpha suite**,
from deployment source `c0fc5217e364a39a4cd123d17a8317c06b80f820`, tree
`6c0ed7b1a5d40662bcd3e124a6d2aedd6447fcf2`. Its five retained EXACT_MATCH explorer
results and scoped authority snapshot at block 26220072 describe those exact
instances. Public funding and activation remain unapproved; Alpha has no global
pause. The directory does not claim a fresh live RPC check.

Jobs' current directory now records the **25 fresh contracts deployed on 18
October 2026**, from source `818b3a246871e4cd4dde86558dbb91ef82b15eef`, tree
`b1c3bb0f4b8d64e0d23376d6b6ef3722c4c67b0d`. The exact public snapshot is pinned to
[publication commit 284351148d96c5390a655aec1f9db806284f2400](https://github.com/MontrealAI/AGIJobsv0/blob/284351148d96c5390a655aec1f9db806284f2400/docs/production/mainnet-2026-10-18/deployment-snapshot.json)
and retained byte for byte as `jobs-mainnet-2026-10-18.json` (SHA-256
`b4335f5763f73e8da664c3cd45ac7ca8fa6f0d3beb2780b209e50fd1e3def23f`). Its
observations include 25 runtime matches, 25 exact source-metadata matches, 46/46
named state checks, eight paused managed modules and no creator ownership among
the 25 contracts. The state anchor is provider-reported finalized block 26221285, hash
`0x4bd7698479db125e9a7e4f031571fd2844224f822a630ba22b40aea48fb592e6`,
at 18:37:11 UTC. Canonicality and provider-finalized status were rechecked;
closeout completed at 18:55:20.035 UTC. Etherscan source readback is separately
timed and explicitly **not block pinned**.

The [dated guide](https://github.com/MontrealAI/AGIJobsv0/blob/284351148d96c5390a655aec1f9db806284f2400/docs/production/mainnet-2026-10-18/README.md), exact public snapshot and
**39 successful historical creator receipts** are retained with original source,
